lines.text: Sweden once made every driver on the road stop dead at ten to five one morning in 1967,
lines.text_kokoro: Sweden once made every driver on the road stop dead at ten to five one morning in nineteen sixty-seven,

lines.text: because at five o'clock, the whole country would switch to driving on the right, like its neighbours, though voters had said no by a landslide.
So when they all switched at once, did road deaths go up, or down?
Ingrid had driven on the left her whole life, and one slip of habit would put her head-on into someone.
They went down, by almost half, because speed limits were cut that morning and everyone drove like a learner,
and for two months, it looked as if Dagen H had made Sweden's roads safer overnight.

lines.text: But by November, the deaths were back where they'd been, because once the road felt normal, the care wore off.
So the safest Ingrid ever drove was the morning she was sure she'd crash.
